summary: No verified counterexample, circular assumption, changed-target defect or high-severity semantic gap found in these 17 frozen contracts. The new network compiler/depth theorem is excluded from this report and reviewed separately.
source_scope: tex/chapters/02_foundations.tex:72-88 DC and dimension-only signed-max supporting steps

model_correspondence.evidence: A Polyhedron is finitely many actual closed affine halfspaces. AffineCover contains finite pieces, slopes, arbitrary biases, global coverage and pointwise affine equality on each cell. CPWL is continuity plus existence of this cover, with no convexity/DC/lattice/network premise.

Local branches are restricted to those active at a point by finite continuity. The one-dimensional endpoint separator follows by an intermediate-value/greatest-zero contradiction. Applying this to the entire affine segment line is valid because the source domain is all real input space. No separation premise is assumed in the lattice theorem.

Blocks are realized subsets of the finite affine-piece type, hence finite despite their existential point witnesses. Each block is nonempty from actual cover equality. Negative max-affine blocks are literal affine minima; separation proves every block below f, and the block at the evaluated point gives equality. Realized-set membership does not contain a representation conclusion.

Polynomial means a nonempty finite max of unrestricted real affine terms. Maximum closure constructs max(g1+h2,g2+h1)-(h1+h2), starting from negative max blocks. The converse uses explicit active-piece polyhedral cells. A directly covered nonconvex cap 3-|x| was checked in Lean without using a pre-existing DC representation to supply CPWL.

Dependence is obtained among slopes in the d-dimensional coordinate space, with zero coefficient sum and nonzero coefficient vector. Its sign is reversed if necessary so the weighted intercept sum is nonpositive. Positive coefficients define A and all remaining terms B; both are nonempty. A fixed partition satisfies min(A)<=max(B) pointwise. This avoids increasing dimension by homogenizing intercepts; arbitrary biases, repeated slopes and zero coefficients are allowed.

The dominated member may depend on the evaluation point, while partition and alternating coefficients are fixed. Pairing powerset subsets containing/omitting that member proves cancellation. The full-maximum coefficient is +/-1; every other restricted maximum contains nonempty B and has strictly fewer terms. Strong induction reaches cardinality <=d+1.

model_correspondence.verdict: helper premise does not contaminate headline
model_correspondence.evidence: finite_representation_of_mem_smallSpan explicitly assumes span membership and extracts a finitely supported sum. That helper assumption is essentially the representation property, but eval_mem_smallSpan independently proves it by the cardinal induction; neither headline assumes it. The final coefficients are real and every indexed maximum nonempty; an empty outer sum is permitted for zero.

boundary_cases: Dimension zero is allowed and each indexed small maximum has exactly one term.
Empty term sets are excluded by Polynomial.inhabited; all recursion bases include nonempty B.
A finite empty affine-piece type cannot cover the inhabited real vector domain.
Ties and duplicate pieces/coefficients need no generic-position hypothesis.
Arbitrary positive and negative intercepts are retained, including in dimension zero.
proof that the cap is not convex
direct composition to arbitrary CPWL signed small maxima
nonvacuous global partition at dimension 1 and 3 terms

independent_experiment.scope: Independent exact finite tests and constructive coefficient producer; not a replacement for the universal Lean proofs.

residual_scope.detail: No ReLU network realization or depth is credited here. New ReLUCompiler and CPWLReLUEquivalence are a separate review requested after this batch.

Existence of a finite real linear combination is proved. No bound on its number of terms, coefficient size, runtime, or executable coefficient extraction is asserted. Classical finite constructions are legitimate for the source existence theorem.
